skill_traces.query:
Jon: Hi Gina! I just wanted to fill you in on my business. Yesterday, I went to a fair to show off my studio, it was both stressful and great! I got some possible leads, so that was awesome. But overall, I've learned that this biz is no cakewalk and having confidence in yourself is important for making it successful!
Gina: Hey Jon, congrats on the fair! It's awesome to see your hard work paying off. Keep on pushing, pal, you're headed for greatness. Oh, and BTW, I started my own online clothing store not so long ago - pretty cool, huh?
Jon: Thanks, Gina! Appreciate your support. Your store looks great, I remember it!
Gina: Thanks, Jon! After losing my job, I wanted to take control of my own destiny and this seemed like the perfect way to do it. It's been a tough journey, but very rewarding.
Jon: Wow, you're awesome for going for it! Setbacks can help us reach our potential, right? I'm having trouble with my business project. Any advice on staying motivated even when times are tough?
Gina: Yeah Jon! Challenges are awesome for learning and growth. To stay motivated, I think of the big goal and why I'm doing it. I also get help from people who support me. And of course, I dance it out. Do you need advice on anything in particular?
Jon: I've been feeling kinda low on confidence lately. It's hard to run a business when you don't have faith in yourself. Any tips on how you stay confident in your business?
Gina: I get it, Jon. Confidence is important in business. I stay motivated by reminding myself of my successes and progress. It also helps to have a good support system. Just focus on why you started this – because you love it! Have faith in yourself, Jon. I do!
Jon: Thanks! Your words mean a lot. Gotta focus on success and why I started. You're right, I love it and that'll keep my confidence up.
Gina: No worries, Jon! Sounds like what I said was helpful. You're incredibly talented and passionate about dance. Don't forget, believe in yourself and your abilities. Tackle any obstacle that comes your way and keep shining!
Jon: Thanks! Your support means a lot. I'm gonna keep going and reach my dreams no matter what.
Gina: Go for it, Jon! You got this! Don't let anything stop you. We're in this together!
Jon: Appreciate your encouragement. We'll keep pushing each other on this path.
Gina: Yeah! Let's keep each other going. We can do it!

selected.name: Extract Offers, Encouragement, and Advice
selected.description: Use during extraction when a message contains one person offering help, giving advice, encouragement, or reassurance to another person.
content: During extraction, treat a single message as sufficient evidence when a speaker offers help, gives advice, encouragement, or reassurance to another person.
Create one event memory capturing the speaker, the recipient, and the gist of what was said, including any explicit guidance or offer topic.
Stop after the gist is captured; do not infer the recipient's internal feelings or expand into multiple memory kinds unless the message contains other distinct facts.
selected.rerank_reason: The session contains multiple instances of Gina offering encouragement and advice to Jon, which directly aligns with the skill's purpose of extracting such interactions.

nearby_not_selected.name: Capture Brief Project Mentions with Full Attributes
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a speaker mentions a project they completed, are working on, or plan to build, even briefly.
content: Create an event candidate for any explicit statement of a completed, ongoing, or planned project, even in small talk.
When several messages describe the same project, consolidate them into one candidate and include every explicit attribute stated.
Stop once the speaker has finished describing the project in that session.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Each Self-Reported Event Separately
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message contains a speaker's explicit first-person past action with a relative time phrase.
content: Treat each explicit first-person past action in a message as a separate event candidate for that speaker.
Resolve the relative time phrase against the message/session timestamp to set world_start.
Do not fold the speaker's action into a candidate about another person or broader theme.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Inspiration and Plan Memories
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a user mentions what inspired or motivated their current or future project.
content: During extraction, treat statements like 'X sparked ideas for my [project]' as a plan/state memory candidate.
Do not skip a turn just because it contains no direct question; extract motivation and project details from casual narrative.
Resolve relative time from the message/session timestamp and include it in the memory.

nearby_not_selected.name: Location Qualifiers for Named Destination Plans
nearby_not_selected.description: When extracting or updating a plan memory that mentions a specific named venue, landmark, or business, include its commonly known location(s) so future location questions can be answered.
content: During extraction, if a plan memory mentions a specific named venue, landmark, or business, add a concise qualifier naming its well-known location(s), e.g., US states or countries.
Use only common knowledge about that entity; do not research or speculate beyond obvious, widely known locations.
If one location is commonly known, record it; if several prominent locations exist, record all commonly known ones, then stop.
Apply the same qualifier when updating an existing plan memory that references the venue.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Start of Specific Creative Work
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a user confirms starting or recently beginning a specific creative work.
content: When a message confirms a user is working on a specific creative work with an ordinal or title and a beginning phrase, add an event memory with subject=user and world_start set to the message date.
Treat recent-start statements as start events; do not mark completion unless explicitly stated.
Prefer this specific event memory over a generic profile enrichment.
